name: tiny_ir
description: Hand-authored labeled retrieval set: 48 short technical passages in 12 topic clusters (4 near-duplicate-topic passages each) and 28 queries with gold passage ids (qrels). Authored for this repo; labels are by construction.
notes: Each query was written from its gold passage(s); relevance labels are by construction and were fixed before any pipeline was run. Query type 'lexical' = shares distinctive terms with the gold passage; 'paraphrase' = same fact, different words. The 4 passages in each topic cluster act as hard negatives for each other.

corpus.text: VACUUM in PostgreSQL reclaims storage occupied by dead tuples left behind by updates and deletes. Autovacuum runs it in the background based on table churn thresholds.
A B-tree index in PostgreSQL speeds up equality and range lookups on a column, at the cost of extra writes on every insert and update.
PostgreSQL write-ahead logging records every change to a log before it is applied to data files, which allows crash recovery by replaying the log.
EXPLAIN ANALYZE executes a PostgreSQL query and reports the actual row counts and timing of each plan node, unlike plain EXPLAIN which only shows estimates.
A Kubernetes Deployment manages a set of identical pods and performs rolling updates, replacing old pods gradually so the service stays available.
A Kubernetes Service gives a stable virtual IP and DNS name to a changing set of pods selected by labels.
The kubelet is the agent on each node that makes sure the containers described in pod specs are running and healthy.
A Kubernetes liveness probe tells the kubelet when to restart a container that has stopped responding, while a readiness probe controls whether it receives traffic.
git rebase replays commits from one branch onto another tip, producing a linear history, but it rewrites commit hashes.
git bisect performs a binary search through commit history to find the commit that introduced a bug.
git stash temporarily shelves uncommitted changes so the working directory is clean, and they can be reapplied later.
git cherry-pick applies the changes introduced by one specific existing commit onto the current branch as a new commit.
The TCP three-way handshake uses SYN, SYN-ACK and ACK segments to establish a connection before data is sent.
UDP is a connectionless transport protocol with no delivery guarantee or retransmission, so it suits low-latency traffic such as DNS lookups and live video.
DNS resolves a hostname such as example.com into an IP address by querying a recursive resolver, which walks root, TLD and authoritative servers.
TLS 1.3 reduces connection setup to one round trip and removes legacy cipher suites such as RSA key exchange.
The Python GIL, or global interpreter lock, lets only one thread execute Python bytecode at a time in CPython, so CPU-bound threads do not run in parallel.
A Python generator uses the yield keyword to produce values lazily one at a time, avoiding the need to hold a full sequence in memory.
Python decorators are functions that wrap another function to add behavior, applied with the @ syntax above the definition.
The asyncio library runs coroutines on a single-threaded event loop and suits I/O-bound workloads such as many concurrent network calls.
A Dockerfile multi-stage build compiles code in one stage and copies only the artifacts into a slim final image, shrinking the image size.
Docker volumes persist data outside a container's writable layer, so the data survives when the container is removed.
Docker Compose describes a multi-container application in a YAML file and starts every service with a single command.
Docker layer caching reuses unchanged image layers on rebuild, so ordering rarely-changing instructions first speeds up builds.
HTTP status 429 Too Many Requests tells a client it has exceeded a rate limit; the Retry-After header may say when to try again.
HTTP status 404 Not Found means the server cannot find the requested resource at the given URL.
HTTP status 503 Service Unavailable indicates the server is temporarily overloaded or down for maintenance.
An idempotent HTTP method such as PUT or DELETE can be repeated with the same effect as a single call, which makes retries safe.
Overfitting happens when a model memorizes noise in the training data and performs much worse on unseen data; regularization and early stopping reduce it.
Precision is the fraction of predicted positives that are truly positive, while recall is the fraction of actual positives that the model finds.
Gradient descent updates model parameters in the direction opposite the gradient of the loss, scaled by a learning rate.
Cross-validation splits data into k folds, training on k-1 folds and validating on the held-out fold, to estimate generalization error.
SQL injection occurs when untrusted input is concatenated into a query string; parameterized queries prevent it by separating code from data.
Cross-site scripting (XSS) injects malicious scripts into pages viewed by other users; output encoding and a content security policy mitigate it.
bcrypt is a deliberately slow password hashing function with a per-password salt and a tunable cost factor.
OAuth 2.0 lets an application obtain limited access to a user's account on another service through access tokens without sharing the user's password.
Double-entry bookkeeping records every transaction as equal debits and credits across accounts, so the books always balance.
A balance sheet reports a company's assets, liabilities and shareholder equity at a single point in time.
Compound interest is calculated on the initial principal and on the interest already accumulated in earlier periods.
The Sharpe ratio measures excess return per unit of volatility, used to compare risk-adjusted performance of investments.
The CAP theorem states that a distributed data store cannot simultaneously guarantee consistency, availability and partition tolerance; during a partition it must trade the first two.
Database sharding splits a large dataset across multiple servers by a shard key, increasing capacity but complicating cross-shard queries.
Redis is an in-memory key-value store often used as a cache, with optional persistence to disk.
A database transaction with ACID properties is atomic, consistent, isolated and durable, so partial failures leave no half-written state.
BM25 ranks documents by term frequency and inverse document frequency with length normalization, rewarding exact keyword matches.
Dense retrieval encodes queries and documents into vectors and ranks by cosine similarity, which captures meaning even when no words overlap.
Reciprocal Rank Fusion merges several ranked lists by summing 1/(k+rank) for each document, requiring no score normalization.
A cross-encoder reranker reads the query and a candidate passage together and outputs a relevance score, which is more accurate but slower than a bi-encoder.
